question: Two events $A$ and $B$ are independent with $P(A)=0.4$ and $P(B)=0.3$. Find the probability that exactly one of the events $A$ and $B$ occurs.
explanation:
Step 1: Probability of simultaneous occurrence
Since $A$ and $B$ are independent, $$P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)=0.4\times0.3=0.12.$$
Step 2: Probability that only $A$ occurs
The event that $A$ occurs but $B$ does not has probability $$P(A\cap B')=P(A)-P(A\cap B)=0.4-0.12=0.28.$$
Step 3: Probability that only $B$ occurs
Similarly, $$P(A'\cap B)=P(B)-P(A\cap B)=0.3-0.12=0.18.$$
Step 4: Probability that exactly one event occurs
The two cases are mutually exclusive. Hence, $$P(\text{exactly one})=0.28+0.18=0.46.$$
Step 5: Conclusion
Therefore, the probability that exactly one of the two independent events occurs is $$\boxed{0.46}.$$
